date: 1950s–present (Mk 80 series); used in Vietnam, Desert Storm and later conflicts
yield_status: Fill is MEASURED: 87 kg (192 lb) tritonal, some sources say 89 kg. TNT equivalent is DISPUTED by metric: RE 1.05 (pressure, Wikipedia RE table) to 1.18 (energy, Tritonal article) gives 91–103 kg. Game uses RE 1.15, so 100 kg = 0.1 t. The task's 0.1 t is correct, not low.
burst_type: CONVENTIONAL_SURFACE (contact with short delay)
paint: Olive drab with a yellow nose band (US HE colour code, NAVEDTRA 14014; Kitty Hawk 1972 photo). Low-drag conical cruciform fin, 2 lugs on top. Variants: Snakeye (4 folding retarder blades), AIR (ballute).
key_timings: Flash 0–10 ms (fireball full size, about 15 m wide, within one frame). Visible shock arc out to about 20–25 m during 0–60 ms. Bright orange ball until about 0.25 s, flame gone by about 0.6 s. Black-grey soil-jet crown peaks at about 35 m wide × 25 m tall at 0.3–1 s. Fragment dust puffs out to 150 m (sparse to 300 m) within 0.1–0.5 s. Dirty thermal cloud top about 60 m at 5 s, 130 m at 30 s, 200 m at 60 s and 290 m at 120 s (Church 1969 measured TNT analogues). No cap or stem.
visual_signature: A sharp white-yellow point flash (aluminium in the tritonal), with an exposure dip of only 1–2 stops. A yellow-orange fireball about 15 m wide appears instantly, edged with black soot within frames. A thin refraction/condensation arc runs ahead to about 20–25 m and a white dust skirt lifts at ground level (all visible in the PD Saber Strike 18 photo). The ball is then swallowed by a ragged black-grey crown of radial soil jets with flying clods, reaching about 35 × 25 m by 1 s, while a ring of fragment dust puffs appears out to about 150 m. Residual orange flame flickers at the base until about 0.6 s. The plume detaches into a lumpy black to grey-brown puff that rises and drifts: about 130 m at 30 s and about 290 m at 2 min. The crater is 7 m wide × 2 m deep with a dark ejecta speckle out to about 25 m. The sound is a single sharp crack.
disputes_resolved: (1) Yield 0.1 t confirmed (91–103 kg range). (2) Fireball: the bombs reference (Ø 15–25 m) and the physics reference (R = 1.0·m^(1/3), Ø 9 m) disagree with the Cooper/HSE fits in LANL LA-14209-T (Ø 15–17 m). Use R = 1.6·W_kg^(1/3), giving Ø 15 m, which a photo confirms. (3) Crater: an instantaneous fuze gives only about 2–4 m (OP 1172 inst. 500-lb GP: 2–3 m). A short delay gives 7–8.5 m (OP 1172 scaled by fill), and Vietnam craters span 3–12 m. Game uses 7 × 2 m with a −0.7 m burst, inside the task's 5–8 m. (4) Fill 87 vs 89 kg: use 87 kg (192 lb). (5) An af.mil caption '7 ft 6.2 in / 18 in diameter' is wrong; use 2.21 m × 0.273 m. (6) Fragment radius: no primary public table was retrieved, so the visual fan is estimated (dense 150 m, sparse 300 m).
blurb_ru: Mk 82 — стандартная американская 500-фунтовая (≈241 кг) авиабомба общего назначения: в строю с 1950-х годов до наших дней, она же — боевая часть управляемых GBU-12 и GBU-38 JDAM. Внутри около 87 кг тритонала (80 % тротила и 20 % алюминиевой пудры), это примерно 0,1 т в тротиловом эквиваленте. Самый слабый взрыв в коллекции и точка отсчёта для всех остальных.
blurb_en: The Mk 82 is the standard US 500-lb (≈241 kg) general-purpose bomb, in service from the 1950s to this day and the warhead of guided weapons such as the GBU-12 and GBU-38 JDAM. It holds about 87 kg of tritonal (80% TNT, 20% aluminium powder), roughly 0.1 t of TNT equivalent. It is the weakest blast in the collection and the yardstick for all the others.

date: 1950s–present; widely used in Vietnam; more than 12,000 expended in Desert Storm (1991)
yield_status: Fill is MEASURED: 429 kg (945 lb) tritonal or H-6. TNT equivalent is DISPUTED by metric: RE 1.05–1.18 gives 450–506 kg. Game uses RE 1.15, giving 493 kg ≈ 0.5 t.
burst_type: CONVENTIONAL_SURFACE (contact with short delay)
paint: Olive drab with a yellow nose band (HE); a blue band means an inert training round. Conical cruciform tail fin (tail span 0.64 m); a 'fat Mk 82' silhouette (Desert Storm photo).
key_timings: Flash 0–15 ms (fireball about 26 m wide within 1–2 frames). Dust shock ring passes about 50 m at 0.05 s and about 100 m at 0.15 s. Bright orange ball until about 0.4 s, with a black cauliflower soot cap forming at 0.1–0.5 s. Flame gone by about 1.0 s. Soil crown and column about 60 m wide × 50 m tall at 1 s. Fragment splash and dust fan dense to 250 m, sparse to 500 m. Cloud top about 100 m at 5 s, 230 m at 30 s, 330 m at 60 s and 440 m at 120 s. Base dust ring 60–80 m.
visual_signature: A hard white-yellow flash (exposure dip about 2 stops), then a bright boiling orange ball about 26 m across. A refraction shell and a clearly visible ring of lifted dust race across dry ground. Within a few tenths of a second black soot rolls up off the top into a black-brown cauliflower cap, while a dark crown of soil jets bursts radially and a wide fan of fragment impacts (dust puffs, or white splashes on water as in the USMC 2007 PD photos) spreads out to about 250 m. Orange flame dies inside a black-brown column about 60 m wide by 1 s, and a tan dust skirt rolls out to about 70 m. The cloud rises as a lumpy wind-sheared dirty thermal (no mushroom): about 230 m at 30 s and about 440 m at 2 min, greying and dropping brown dust downwind. It leaves a 13 m × 4 m crater with a raised rim and clods thrown to 30–50 m. The sound is a deep, heavy boom with a short rumble.
disputes_resolved: (1) Length: FAS/GlobalSecurity 129 in (3.28 m) and a USAF caption 10 ft 9 in agree; Wikipedia's 3.84 m is the outlier. Use 3.28 m. (2) Crater: Wikipedia's '50 ft wide, 36 ft deep' is unsourced and the depth is implausible. OP 1172 (2,000-lb GP with an equal TNT fill) gives 12.5–16.5 m × 3.4–5.2 m for a short delay and 3.4–4.6 × 1.2 m for an instantaneous fuze, and CNN/Synthetaic attribute Gaza craters ≥12 m to 2,000-lb bombs. Use 13 × 4 m. (3) Fireball: the bombs reference Ø 40–60 m is too large. Cooper/HSE fits give Ø 25–29 m. Use R = 13 m. (4) Lethal fragment radius: Wikipedia says 120 m and others say 366 m or more. The game uses a visual fan (250 m dense, 500 m sparse), not a lethality claim.
blurb_ru: Mk 84 — самая тяжёлая бомба американской серии Mk 80: около 925 кг, из них 429 кг тритонала, то есть примерно 0,5 т в тротиловом эквиваленте. На её основе сделаны управляемые GBU-10, GBU-24 и GBU-31 JDAM, а только за «Бурю в пустыне» (1991) было сброшено больше 12 000 таких бомб. При подрыве с небольшим замедлением в мягком грунте она оставляет воронку 12–15 м в поперечнике.
blurb_en: The Mk 84 is the heaviest member of the US Mk 80 family: about 925 kg, including 429 kg of tritonal, or roughly 0.5 t of TNT equivalent. It is the basis of the GBU-10, GBU-24 and GBU-31 JDAM guided bombs, and more than 12,000 were dropped in Desert Storm (1991) alone. With a short fuze delay in soft ground it leaves a crater 12–15 m across.

date: 1944–1945 (first use Saumur tunnel 8/9 June 1944; Tirpitz sunk 12 Nov 1944); 854 dropped
yield_status: Fill is MEASURED: 5,200 lb (2,359 kg) Torpex D1. TNT equivalent is DISPUTED: RE 1.30 (Wikipedia RE table) gives 3.07 t, while 1.5–1.6 (Torpex article; RN torpedo paper, an underwater basis) gives 3.5–3.8 t. Game uses 3.1 t. Because the burst is buried, the effective air-blast yield is about 0.2 t (ESTIMATED).
burst_type: CONVENTIONAL_BURIED (deep penetration; camouflet-type)
paint: Undocumented. Photos (B&W, IWM CH 15363/CH 15380) show a uniformly dark body (probably RAF bronze-green class colour), a thin light ring near the sharp ogive nose, a 'TORPEX D1' stencil, a long tapering aluminium tail cone (about half the length) and 4 fins offset about 5° to spin the bomb. Game: dark olive/bronze-green body, light grey nose ring, white stencil.
key_timings: Impact at about 335 m/s (750 mph) after a fall of about 37 s, with a soil puff 5–10 m high; the game detonates 1.5 s later. T+0: no flash. Ground shock reaches the surface in 10–20 ms, with a spall dust ring out to 40–60 m and camera tremor. A dome heaves 3–6 m high and 30–40 m wide at 0.05–0.4 s. It vents at 0.3–1 s into a spiky dark soil and grey-white smoke geyser that reaches 60–120 m by 2–3 s. Fallback and a brown base surge out to 100–200 m at 2–6 s. Possible slumping into the cavity during 3–10 s. Brown-grey cloud about 180 m at 30 s and about 300 m at 2 min. Tremor felt before the muffled air thump.
visual_signature: Almost no fire. The bomb strikes near-vertically with a small sharp puff and disappears into the ground. A beat later the whole patch of ground jumps: a ring of dust leaps up out to about 50 m, the camera shakes, and a dome of earth 30–40 m wide bulges and cracks with dust spurting from the cracks. The dome tears open into a geyser of dark brown-black soil and grey-white smoke with spiky radial jets and big clods and blocks on ballistic arcs (compare the PD IWM C 4775 photo of a shore Tallboy burst at Tirpitz). At most a dull red glimmer shows in the vent for a few frames. The column tops out at about 60–120 m, then collapses as a curtain of fallback, and a low brown base surge rolls out to about 100–200 m. The dust thins to reveal a crater about 30 m wide and about 10 m deep with a 1.5–2 m lip and a bright fresh-soil apron (Saumur reconnaissance photo). The ground may keep slumping into the cavity for seconds. A dirty brown-grey cloud drifts up to about 300 m. The tremor arrives before a muffled heavy thump, followed by a long rumble of falling debris.
disputes_resolved: (1) Crater width about 30 m is confirmed by at least two independent sources: Wikipedia/GlobalSecurity/hmdb give 100 ft, and the IBCC Saumur reconnaissance caption gives 100–110 ft. (2) Crater depth '80 ft (24 m)' is unsourced and implausible for an apparent crater; a forum report of the Ashley Walk test gives 130 × 30 ft. Use 10 m and treat 24 m as burst depth plus the disturbed zone. (3) Burst depth: Saumur's '60 ft (18 m) below the surface' gives −18 m. A deeper burst (more than about 25–30 m) would make a pure camouflet with subsidence only, which could be an optional variant. (4) Impact speed: 750 mph (Wikipedia, Bomber Command Museum of Canada) is correct; GlobalSecurity's '3,600–3,700 ft/s' is an error. (5) Mass: 5,377–5,443 kg, use 5,400 kg. (6) Yield: 3.1 t at RE 1.3. (7) Paint is undocumented; the game choice is stated as a design decision. (8) The 2020 Świnoujście water-column height was never measured ('hundreds of feet'), so it is used only as a blurb fact.
blurb_ru: Tallboy — британская 12 000-фунтовая (≈5,4 т) «сейсмическая» бомба конструктора Барнса Уоллиса с 2,4 т торпекса (≈3 т в тротиловом эквиваленте). Сброшенная с высоты около 5,5 км, она врезалась в землю на скорости около 1200 км/ч и взрывалась глубоко под поверхностью, обрушивая цели: так в 1944 году были завалены железнодорожный тоннель в Сомюре и потоплен линкор «Тирпиц». За войну сбросили 854 такие бомбы, а одна неразорвавшаяся сдетонировала под водой в польском Свиноуйсьце в 2020 году.
blurb_en: Tallboy was Barnes Wallis's British 12,000-lb (≈5.4 t) "earthquake bomb", filled with 2.4 t of Torpex (about 3 t of TNT equivalent). Dropped from about 5.5 km, it struck the ground at roughly 1,200 km/h and exploded deep underground, bringing targets down from below: in 1944 it blocked the Saumur railway tunnel and sank the battleship Tirpitz. 854 were dropped during the war, and an unexploded one detonated underwater at Świnoujście, Poland, in 2020.

name_en: Grand Slam (22,000 lb MC deep-penetration bomb)
date: 13 March 1945 (Ashley Walk test); first combat use 14 March 1945, Bielefeld viaduct
yield_status: ESTIMATED: 6.5 long tons (6.6 t) TNT per Wikipedia; cross-check 4,300 kg Torpex x 1.5 = 6.45 t
burst_type: buried (delayed-fuze deep penetration, camouflet/earthquake effect)
paint: Museum (RAF Museum London, CC0 photo): deep bronze-green body, pale-blue band and thin red ring on the nose. Wartime photo CH15369: darker forward body, lighter aft body/tail. Test bomb: black-and-white. Game: dark bronze-green with blue band and red ring.
key_timings: t0 detonation at -20 m: seismic jolt first; 0-0.3 s ground dome 35-40 m wide, 5-8 m high; 0.3-1 s dome ruptures, radial jets of dark earth and grey gas (optional dull vent glint <=0.2 s); 1-4 s ejecta column 150-250 m, cauliflower top about 130 m wide; 4-30 s fallback and a 300-400 m dust cloud drifting; minutes later gas puffs venting from the crater. Air shock is weak; at 5 km it arrives after about 14.6 s.
visual_signature: No fireball: the 'earthquake bomb'. The dark-green 7.8 m bomb falls nearly vertically at about 320 m/s and buries itself with a dust puff. Detonation shows first as a ground jolt and ripple ring. The surface heaves into a 35-40 m dome that bursts at 0.3-1 s into radial jets of dark brown soil and grey-white gas, forming the dark radial streaks seen in the Arnsberg 1945 photo. A 150-250 m brown-grey ejecta column with a light-grey billowing top about 130 m wide rises in 1-4 s. Clods fall back over 150-200 m and a tan dust cloud 300-400 m high drifts away. The crater left behind is 38 m across, 10 m deep, with a raised lip, and gas keeps puffing out 'like a volcano' (eyewitness). Earth-tone palette, no thermal flash, deep low thump.
disputes_resolved: Length 7.75-7.8 m vs 8.08 m: use 7.8 m (2 of 3 figures). Diameter 1.17 m (Wikipedia's 0.94 m misreads 3 ft 10 in). Ashley Walk crater 38 x 10 m (witness/Wikipedia/Bomber Command Museum) vs 40 x 21 m (Geograph/Dambusters blog) vs 43 x 21 m: use 38 x 10 m, which is consistent with cube-root cratering for 6.6 t. Number dropped 42 vs 41: use 42. No source supports an 'orange flash'; treat as no fireball.
blurb_ru: Британская «сейсмическая» бомба Барнса Уоллиса массой 10 тонн, самая тяжёлая авиабомба Второй мировой. Она падала почти со скоростью звука, уходила глубоко в грунт и взрывалась под землёй: 4,3 т торпекса (≈6,5 т в тротиловом эквиваленте) выбивали опору из-под цели. 14 марта 1945 года первая боевая «Гранд Слэм» обрушила пролёты виадука в Билефельде; до конца войны их сбросили 42.
blurb_en: Barnes Wallis's 10-tonne British 'earthquake bomb', the heaviest bomb dropped in the Second World War. It fell at nearly the speed of sound, burrowed deep into the ground and exploded underneath its target: 4.3 t of Torpex (about 6.5 t of TNT) knocked the ground out from under it. On 14 March 1945 the first operational Grand Slam brought down spans of the Bielefeld viaduct; 42 were dropped before the war ended.

date: Live tests 11 March 2003 and 21 November 2003 (Eglin AFB); combat use 13 April 2017, 19:32 local, Achin, Nangarhar, Afghanistan
yield_status: MEASURED/ESTIMATED consistent: 11 t TNT (Wikipedia); 8,500 kg H-6 x 1.35 = 11.5 t (AF Armament Museum factor)
burst_type: low airburst just above ground (proximity fuze), conventional aluminised HE (not fuel-air)
paint: 11 Mar 2003 test article bright orange with black stripes (DoD photo). 21 Nov 2003 test bomb dark olive/grey (USAF video). Eglin museum display bright green with yellow nose and white MOAB letters. Game: dark olive-grey with yellow nose band; orange test scheme optional.
key_timings: t0 one-frame blue-white flash (<=33-50 ms); 0.03-0.15 s yellow-white hemispherical dome spreading sideways; about 0.45 s maximum flattened dome about 140 m wide x 40 m tall (aspect about 3.5-4:1); 0.5-1.5 s orange to orange-red with brown/grey smoke blotches, dust skirt racing out (about 250 m wide at 3 s); 2-2.5 s last flames; 3-10 s white/light-grey cauliflower cloud, about 120 m tall by 8 s; 10 s-3 min thermal rises to about 1.5 km, cap about 0.5 km, no true stem. Sound at 8 km after about 23 s. Times measured from the USAF video timecode.
visual_signature: A broad, low, golden pancake of flame that turns white. The 9.2 m olive bomb drops nose-down on grid fins and bursts about 2 m above the ground. After a single blue-white flash, a brilliant yellow-white dome spreads sideways far faster than it rises, flattening to about 140 m wide and 40 m tall within about 0.45 s, with a turbulent lumpy surface, white core and orange rim. It fades to orange-red with brown-grey smoke patches by 1.5 s while a ground-level dust ring and shock skirt race outward. Flames are gone by about 2.5 s and the cloud becomes white to light grey (aluminium oxide plus dust), not black, billowing into a stemless cauliflower thermal about as tall as wide at 8 s. It then rises over minutes to about 1.5 km. No crater: a scorched, scoured disc 150-250 m wide with flattened vegetation.
disputes_resolved: Cloud top: the '10,000 ft' figure is press-reported and partly a pre-test expectation; a Pentagon official said the cloud was a tall debris cloud, not a nuclear-style mushroom. Use 1.5 km, scaled by heat release (Q^1/4) from the measured Little Feller I/II clouds (1.8 km AGL for 18-22 t nuclear). Fireball: my frame measurement of the 2003 video gives 120-170 m wide x 30-45 m tall; Alcis's 140 m radius (Afghanistan) is an upper bound that likely includes the scorch zone. Use half-width 70 m, height 40 m. Smoke is white/grey, not the black TNT palette. Mechanism is conventional HE, not fuel-air (Scientific American is wrong). The 11 Mar 2003 test used tritonal; production weapons use H-6. Burst height about 2 m (Business Insider estimate of 6 ft; consistent with the video).
blurb_ru: GBU-43/B MOAB — управляемая авиабомба ВВС США массой 9,8 т с 8,5 т взрывчатки H-6 (≈11 т в тротиловом эквиваленте), самый мощный неядерный боеприпас, когда-либо применённый в бою. Её выталкивают из грузового отсека транспортника MC-130 на платформе с вытяжным парашютом, а взрывается она у самой земли и почти не оставляет воронки. Испытана во Флориде в 2003 году (облако видели за 30 км), в бою применена один раз — 13 апреля 2017 года против туннелей ИГИЛ в Афганистане.
blurb_en: The GBU-43/B MOAB is a 9.8-tonne US guided bomb carrying 8.5 t of H-6 explosive (about 11 t of TNT), the most powerful non-nuclear weapon ever used in combat. It is pushed out of the cargo ramp of an MC-130 on a parachute-extracted pallet, explodes just above the ground and leaves almost no crater. It was tested in Florida in 2003 (the cloud was seen 20 miles away) and used in combat once, on 13 April 2017, against ISIS tunnels in Afghanistan.

name_en: W54 Davy Crockett (test Little Feller I)
date: 17 July 1962, 10:00 PDT (17:00 GMT), NTS Area 18, Nevada
yield_status: DISPUTED (minor): DOE/NV-209 gives only 'Low'; 18 t per Sublette/Wikipedia; 20 t programmed/nominal (Hansen; 1961 Safety Rules). Game 18 t.
burst_type: near-surface low airburst (fired projectile)
paint: Not documented. 1961 B&W photos show a dark body and lighter fins; museum replicas are olive drab. Game: olive drab body, light-grey fins, natural-metal piston rod.
key_timings: t0 blue-white point, full camera white-out for about 0.1-0.17 s (film); second thermal peak about 6 ms; hemispherical fireball R about 17 m by about 0.03-0.05 s; glow yellow to orange-red until about 0.6 s, with a bright dust band spreading along the ground; 0.6-1.5 s white bell-shaped cloud on the ground; 1.5-20 s column lifts off, thin dusty stem, cap about 0.7 km at 20 s; 40 s cap tilted drifting NNW; about 3 min top stabilises at 11,000 ft MSL = about 1.8 km above ground. Sound at 3.5 km (observers) about 10 s, at 8 km about 23 s.
visual_signature: The smallest nuclear event: tiny but blinding, with a cloud far bigger than its fireball. Setting is a morning high desert (1,578 m) with sagebrush and a dirt road through GZ, wind toward the NNW at about 7 m/s. A finned 'atomic watermelon' arcs 2.85 km from an M113 and bursts 0.9 m above the ground. A blue-white flash whites out the view for about 0.15 s, then a hemispherical fireball about 17 m in radius glows white-yellow and cools to orange-red by about 0.6 s. A bright ring of dust erupts at its base and the road dust lights up as a bright horizontal line. It becomes a boiling white/grey bell-shaped cloud 40-60 m tall, which lifts into a narrow column with a balled head on a thin, wavy, dusty stem (Ivy Flats film; DNA 6027F fig. 8-1 at 20 s). The cap, white above and tan dust below, leans and drifts NNW and tops out at about 1.8 km above the desert after about 3 minutes. On the ground: a shallow crater about 8 m, a scorched disc 30-40 m, and blown-down sagebrush to 100-200 m.
disputes_resolved: Burst height RESOLVED to 3 ft (0.9 m): DOE/NV-209 Rev 16 (HOB 3), DOE/NV-1200 and DNA 6027F all say 3 ft. DNA 6027F explains the shot was originally planned at 40 ft and 'changed to a three-foot shot'; Wikipedia's 20-40 ft and Sublette's 40 ft are the pre-shot plan or the fuze's 40 ft option. Yield: use 18 t (20 t nominal). Cloud top 11,000 ft is MSL (DNA 6027F convention; GZ 5,178 ft), so about 1.8 km AGL, not 3.35 km; Little Feller II matches. Firing distance is 2,853 m (DNA 6027F; Brookings 9,357 ft), not the 852 m in 01_BOMBS_REFERENCE (DOE/NV-1200's '2,796 feet' is a unit slip). The sub-kt cloud formula in 02_PHYSICS (0.72 km) under-predicts the measured 1.8 km.
blurb_ru: 17 июля 1962 года на Невадском полигоне солдаты армии США выстрелили боевым ядерным снарядом M388 с боеголовкой W54 из безоткатного орудия «Дэви Крокетт», установленного на бронетранспортёре. «Атомный арбуз» массой около 34 кг пролетел 2,85 км и взорвался менее чем в метре над землёй с мощностью около 18 т в тротиловом эквиваленте; облако поднялось примерно на 1,8 км над пустыней. Испытание Little Feller I стало последним атмосферным ядерным взрывом на Невадском полигоне; за ним наблюдали Роберт Кеннеди и генерал Максвелл Тейлор.
blurb_en: On 17 July 1962, US Army soldiers at the Nevada Test Site fired a live M388 projectile with a W54 warhead from a Davy Crockett recoilless gun mounted on an armoured personnel carrier. The 34 kg 'atomic watermelon' flew 2.85 km and exploded less than a metre above the ground with a yield of about 18 tons of TNT; its cloud rose about 1.8 km above the desert. Little Feller I was the last atmospheric nuclear explosion at the Nevada Test Site, watched by Robert F. Kennedy and General Maxwell Taylor.

date: 2007-09-11 (date of the TV broadcast; test site not named)
yield_status: CLAIMED by Russia (44 t TNT, 'four times MOAB'); not independently verified. Experts doubt it: Coyle put it at no more than about 1.5x MOAB (~15-17 t), and Lange said the visible blast looks too small.
burst_type: thermobaric / fuel-air: the aerosol cloud spreads near the ground and is then detonated
paint: Not documented. Game: matt grey-green or light grey with no markings. Shape after Wired 2007: stubby cylinder with domed ends, two ski-like skids, drogue chute on top/rear. Dimensions are ESTIMATED.
key_timings: Parachute descent. 0-0.15 s: grey aerosol pancake, about 100 m wide and 10-15 m thick. 0.15-0.25 s: whole cloud flashes yellow-white. 0.25-1.5 s: flattened rolling flame dome grows to ~120 m across and ~70 m tall, with a dust ring racing outward. 1.5-5 s: orange to red with black soot; it lifts into a short-stemmed mushroom. 5-8 s: flames out. Smoke reaches ~2 km at ~3 min. Sound at 10 km arrives after ~29 s. Claimed destruction ring 300 m; physics gives 5 psi at ~250-300 m and 1 psi at ~0.78 km.
visual_signature: A fuel-air explosion, not a nuclear one: a broad, flat, ground-hugging, turbulent yellow-orange flame dome (~120 m across, up to 160 m) instead of a smooth sphere. Little exposure blow-out. The flame turns orange-red with heavy black soot rolls inside, rolls into a short mushroom/torus within ~5 s, and dies by ~8 s, leaving a dark grey-black smoke ball rising to ~2 km. Tan dust ring and shock shimmer on flat plain. Palette: flash #FFF4C8, flame #FFB030/#FF7A10, smoke #2A2522, dust #B59A78.
disputes_resolved: Yield: use the claimed 44 t, labelled 'заявлено, не подтверждено'. Mass 7.1 t vs ~8 t: use 7.1 t. The 6,350 kg figure in 01_BOMBS_REFERENCE.md was not found in any source, so drop it. The narration says air burst but the footage looks like a ground blast; this fits a fuel-air cloud lying near the ground, so use a 10 m burst. The '300 m radius' and '20x area' claims contradict each other; show only the 300 m ring, which matches physics for 44 t. Fireball size and duration are estimated by fuel-cloud scaling (CBU-72 scaled gives ~107 m; CCPS 5.8*M^(1/3) gives 111 m and 0.45*M^(1/3) gives 8.6 s).
blurb_ru: 11 сентября 2007 г. российское ТВ показало испытание «авиационной вакуумной бомбы повышенной мощности». Заявлено около 7 т взрывчатки и 44 т в тротиловом эквиваленте — вчетверо больше американской MOAB. Независимо это не подтверждено: в смонтированном ролике бомба и самолёт ни разу не показаны в одном кадре.
blurb_en: On 11 September 2007 Russian TV showed a test of an "aviation vacuum bomb of increased power". Russia claimed about 7 t of explosive and a 44-ton TNT equivalent, four times America's MOAB. None of this has been independently confirmed: in the heavily edited video the bomb and the bomber never appear in the same shot.

date: never tested; production Nov 2021 - 18 Dec 2024
yield_status: ESTIMATED / unofficial. NNSA says only 'substantial reduction in yield'. FAS/NWA give settings of 0.3 / (1.5) / 10 / 50 kt. 0.3 kt is the commonly cited minimum; the 1.5 kt setting for the -12 specifically is weakly sourced.
burst_type: air burst (conceptual), desert test range
paint: War-reserve finish is not public. The only documented look is the official flight-test livery: white/light-grey nose and tail, red-orange centre section, guided tail kit with 4 small fins.
key_timings: Thermal minimum 1.2 ms (R~17 m). Breakaway ~1.8 ms. Second maximum 23 ms. Max fireball 38 m at ~0.15 s. Glow red by ~0.5 s and faded by ~1 s. Red-brown cloud ball rises at 30-40 m/s; z/H is 0.27 at 17 s, 0.67 at 60 s and 1.0 at ~4 min (2.0 km above burst). Blast: 5 psi 0.48 km, 1 psi 1.47 km. 3rd-degree burns 0.41 km. Sound at 12 km after ~35 s.
visual_signature: A small, quick nuclear airburst. Blue-white flash and white-out, brief dim orange shell, then a brilliant white sphere 60-75 m across that never touches the ground at 150 m. It goes yellow, orange and dull red within ~1 s. A low tan precursor dust skirt spreads on the desert, and a shock shimmer runs out with a Mach-stem kink. Then a compact, lumpy reddish-brown (NO2) cloud ball (Able colour photo) rises with a thin separate dust column below that does not join it (Wasp). It becomes a small grey-white cap ~0.9 km wide at ~2 km above the burst after ~4 min. Palette: #FFFFFF, #FFE08A, #FF9A3C, #B5401E, cloud #7A3B22 to #C9C4BC, dust #C8B28E.
disputes_resolved: No official yield numbers exist, so use the 0.3 kt estimate and badge it as a modelled burst. Burst height: 150 m instead of the 100 m in 01_BOMBS_REFERENCE.md, because 150 m matches the scaled height of Teapot Wasp (1.2 kt at 232 m) and Tumbler-Snapper Able (1 kt at 242 m), so their real photos are valid references. Fireball 38 m instead of 40-55 m (that range is for 1 kt). Cloud height comes only from scaling (2.7*W^0.33 km gives 1.8 km; scaling from 1-kt clouds gives 1.8-2.4 km), so use 2.0 km above the burst.
blurb_ru: B61-12 — американская авиабомба с управляемым хвостовым блоком и выбираемой мощностью: длина ≈3,7 м, масса ≈374 кг, выпускалась в 2021–2024 гг. Официально мощности засекречены; по независимым оценкам минимальная — около 0,3 кт, максимальная — около 50 кт. Ни одна B61-12 никогда не взрывалась: здесь показана расчётная модель взрыва 0,3 кт, построенная по испытаниям 1950-х годов.
blurb_en: The B61-12 is a US gravity bomb with a guided tail kit and selectable yield: about 3.7 m long, about 374 kg, produced in 2021–2024. Its yields are classified; independent estimates put the lowest setting near 0.3 kt and the highest near 50 kt. No B61-12 has ever been detonated, so this is a modelled 0.3 kt burst based on 1950s test data.

yield_status: DISPUTED, resolved. Estimates: LANL 1985 15 kt +/-20%; DS86 15 kt; DS02 16 kt; Penney 12 +/-1 kt; 1960s 16.6 kt; Truman 1945 said 20 kt. Use 15 kt (UI: ≈15 кт, оценки 12–18).
burst_type: air burst over a city
paint: Not documented in primary sources. B&W photos show a dark, smooth, semi-gloss casing with stencilled numbers and chalked messages; replicas are dark olive drab. Game: dark olive-drab/gunmetal, semi-gloss, white stencils, open box tail, top lug, small whip antennas on the upper rear body.
key_timings: Fall 43-44 s from ~9.45 km. Fireball R: ~30 m at 1 ms; 81 m at the thermal minimum (8.5 ms); 90 m at breakaway (13 ms); ~135 m at the second maximum (0.13 s, ~7,700 °C); 190 m at ~1 s. Main heat on the ground 0.2-3 s. Shock at the hypocentre ~1.3 s; 2 km 3.9 s; 5 km 12 s; 20 km ~55 s. Cloud: 1.6 km at 18 s, 3.4 km at 42 s, 6.1 km at ~90 s (NARA '20,000 ft'), 9 km at ~3 min, 12.5 km at ~10 min. Enola Gay at 18.5 km felt 2 jolts (direct plus ground-reflected). Fires within minutes; firestorm peak 10:00-15:00 over ~11 km2. Black rain from ~20 min-1 h to the NW; heavy-rain oval 19x11 km; traces until ~15-16 h.
visual_signature: Seen from 20 km: instant blue-white white-out ('pika'), brief dim orange shell, then a brilliant white sphere growing to ~380 m across at 1 s, high above the city (600 m), with no ground contact. Heat pulse and smoking ground for ~3 s. It goes yellow, orange and dull red as it rises and roils into a torus. Caron saw the shock as a ring on the ground that was really a sphere rising toward the plane, 'like dropping a pebble in a still pond'. The cloud is white outside, purplish-black inside with a fiery red core, and boils upward into a white cauliflower cap with a grey stem. A low black-brown boiling layer of dust and smoke spreads ~3 km over the city and into the foothills, with fires springing up. The cap reaches ~12.5 km, ~4.5 km wide, at ~10 min. Optional late phase: firestorm pyrocumulus and black sticky rain drifting NW.
disputes_resolved: Burst height 580 vs 600 m: 580 m is the fuze setting and the DS86 value; DS02 (RERF, 2002) revised it to 600 m, so use 600 m. Yield: 15 kt (LANL/DS86) vs 16 kt (DS02) changes the fireball radius by only ~2.6%, so use 15 kt. Fireball: the 280 m figure is Nagasaki's; Hiroshima City says a radius over 200 m at 1 s; Wikipedia says 370 m across; the formula gives 360 m across. Use R=190 m. Cloud: '3 km at 48 s' fits the physics curve; '9 km at 8.5 min' is wrong and should be ~3 min. Crew saw it ~10,000 ft above their 31,000 ft (~12.5 km). 16 km is a high-uncertainty 2010 photo analysis and ~8 km an older city estimate. Romps et al. 2026 give ≥11.3 km at 97 min (cloud remnant plus fire plume). Use 12.5 km at 10 min. Shocks: two (Caron, DOE), not three (509th narrative only). The famous tall broad photo is the firestorm cloud hours later, not the mushroom cloud.
blurb_ru: 6 августа 1945 г. в 8:15 бомбардировщик B-29 «Энола Гэй» сбросил «Малыша» на Хиросиму; примерно через 44 с бомба взорвалась на высоте около 600 м. Мощность — около 15 кт (оценки 12–18 кт), через секунду огненный шар достиг почти 400 м в поперечнике, а облако за несколько минут поднялось примерно на 12 км. Пожары и «чёрный дождь» последовали в первые часы; к концу 1945 г. погибли около 140 000 человек.
blurb_en: At 8:15 on 6 August 1945 the B-29 Enola Gay dropped Little Boy on Hiroshima; about 44 seconds later it exploded roughly 600 m above the city. The yield was about 15 kt (estimates 12–18 kt); within a second the fireball grew to nearly 400 m across, and within minutes the cloud rose to about 12 km. Fires and "black rain" followed within hours, and about 140,000 people had died by the end of 1945.

date: 1953-05-25 08:30:00 PDT (15:30 UTC), Frenchman Flat, Nevada Test Site Area 5 (site elevation 938 m)
yield_status: MEASURED, official DOE 15 kt (predicted 14 kt); 4 sources agree
burst_type: low airburst (gun-fired shell, time fuze); scaled height 212 ft/kt^(1/3), inside the precursor regime
paint: not documented; designer choice (olive drab, like the M65 gun, is plausible)
key_timings: Fired 08:29:41, burst 19 s later. Fireball radius about 510*t^0.4 m: 32 m @1 ms, 81 m @10 ms. First thermal minimum 13.3-14.9 ms (measured). Shock reaches the ground at GZ at about 55 ms. Reflected shock hits the fireball bottom at 0.07 s and flattens it by 0.10 s (measured). Second maximum at 122-138 ms with R about 170 m (measured). Mach stem from about 160 m ground range at about 0.13 s. Precursor dust wall 30-100 m high from 0.15 to 3 s, out to about 1.6 km. Shock at the 4.57 km trenches about 11 s, at the gun (10-11 km) about 28-30 s. Cloud top AGL: 4.1 km @1 min, 6.1 @2, 8.4 @4, 9.6 @6, 9.7 @7 (35 kft MSL), max about 10.0 @9 min; base 6.1 km AGL.
visual_signature: Low, dusty, sheared airburst over a pale dry lake on a clear morning (sun 34 deg up in the E, cirrus). Blue-white flash, then the ball dims to an opaque orange-red at 14 ms. The ground under it popcorns and fumes; black and white smoke screens and smoke-rocket trails are props. At 0.07-0.10 s a pale reflected-shock dome rises under the ball and flattens its bottom. At 0.13 s the ball is white-yellow, R about 170 m, and nearly touches the ground. A Mach stem forms about 160 m out. A ragged precursor dust wall 30-100 m high races ahead of the main front to about 1.5 km, and smoke trails kink as it passes. The fireball is 'not as colorful' and fades fast: yellow then orange in 1-5 s. An orange-brown cap with a glowing orange toroid forms over a thick dark-brown dust stem and a wide white-grey dust skirt. The cloud reaches 9.7 km AGL at 7 min (base 6.1 km) and turns white-grey. Very strong SW winds (90-140 mph aloft) shear it and carry it NE quickly. Three successive ice caps form an 'ice skirt' on the column. No crater; a dust storm lingers.
disputes_resolved: Precursor is documented by Wikipedia, DNA 6014F (Project 8.12b precursor panels at Encore/Grable, smoke-screen tests), Glasstone (scaled HOB 212 ft is far below the 800 ft limit; precursor ends below about 6 psi, about 1.6 km) and secondary damage accounts. Mach-stem start follows Glasstone's rule (ground range about HOB); the triple-point height curve is an estimate. Cloud top 35,000 ft MSL (Clark 1954 via DRI 2020 report, and the DASA 1251 Fig. 105 rise curve) = 9.7 km AGL. The physics-doc t_min formula is too early: measured 13.3-14.9 ms, so recommend 0.0036*W^0.5 s. Miss-distance figures differ between sources (86 ft W/136 ft S vs 45 ft W/162 ft short), which is irrelevant to the game.
blurb_ru: 25 мая 1953 года 280-мм пушка M65 «Atomic Annie» выстрелила ядерным снарядом мощностью 15 кт над пустыней Френчмен-Флэт в Неваде. Через 19 секунд снаряд взорвался в 160 м над землёй, более чем в 10 км от орудия. Это единственный ядерный снаряд в истории, действительно выпущенный из пушки. Низкий взрыв над раскалённой пустыней породил «предвестник» — пыльную ударную волну, которая обогнала основную и разбила технику сильнее, чем ожидали.
blurb_en: On 25 May 1953 the 280 mm M65 "Atomic Annie" cannon fired a 15-kiloton nuclear shell over Frenchman Flat, Nevada. The shell burst 19 seconds later, 160 m above the ground and more than 10 km from the gun. It is the only nuclear shell ever actually fired from a gun. The low burst over hot desert produced a "precursor", a dust-laden shock front that outran the main blast wave and wrecked vehicles worse than expected.

date: 1945-07-16 05:29:45 MWT (11:29:45 UTC); Jornada del Muerto, New Mexico (site elevation 1,409 m). Pre-dawn: sun -7.5 deg at azimuth 58 deg, sunrise 06:07
yield_status: DISPUTED. Official DOE 21 kt (1945 value 18.6 kt, revised 1963). Other estimates: Taylor 16.8, Hanson 2016 22.1, Selby/LANL 2021 24.8 +/- 2 kt. Low values: blast gauges about 10 kt, Fermi about 10 kt, 2026 preprint 9.1 +/- 4.5 kt (core-only, unreviewed). Game value 21 kt.
burst_type: tower shot (near-surface; scaled HOB about 11 m/kt^(1/3)); device in a sheet-metal shed atop a 100 ft steel tower
paint: unpainted bare metal assembly with cables, in a corrugated sheet-metal shed (dimensions and mass are estimates; not well documented)
key_timings: Taylor/Mack measured radius (m): 11.1 @0.1 ms, 31 @0.65 ms (ground contact), 36 @0.94 ms, 49 @1.9 ms, 67 @4.6 ms, 106 @15 ms, 130 @25 ms, 145 @34 ms, 175 @53 ms, 185 @62 ms; Mack fit R = 564*(t+0.0004)^0.4 (216 m @90 ms). Spikes and blisters 0.1-2 ms; lumpy ground skirt and Mach belt from about 2 ms; Mach belt visible to about 100 ms; curtain line 3-11 ms. Breakaway / thermal minimum at about 16 ms (105 m). Dark NOx front 32 ms to 0.85 s (375 m); shock invisible at 0.10 s (240 m). Second maximum about 0.15 s (est.). Ball about 300 m radius by 1-2 s; top starts rising at 2 s; neck and vortex ring at 3.5 s; bright glow about 15 s; dull red about 30 s, then purple glow about 5 s. Cloud top rises at 57 m/s to 1.5 km (about 26 s). Shock arrives at 9.1 km about 27 s, 16 km about 44 s, 32 km about 92 s. Cloud top AGL (DASA): 2.1 km @1 min, 3.3 @2, 5.3 @4, 6.9 @6, 8.2 @8, 9.5 @10, still rising; game final 10.5 km at about 11-12 min; base 1.8 km AGL. Sun reaches the cloud top at about 05:51.
visual_signature: Pre-dawn scene: deep blue-violet sky, pale band low in the ENE, broken cloud overhead after rain, dark desert, 30 m tower with a tin shed. A violet/blue-white flash turns twilight into 'brighter than midday' for 1-2 s. A blistered bubble with short spikes below the equator touches the ground at 0.65 ms and becomes a smooth mottled hemisphere. A curtain line sweeps up the dome at 3-11 ms. A bright lumpy 'popcorn' skirt and a smooth Mach belt hug the base. The dome is about 220 m wide at 16 ms and dims to orange-red at the thermal minimum (about 16 ms). A dark NOx front rides behind the shock. Then a white second peak, yellowing, as the hemisphere grows to about 600 m wide by 1-2 s while dust eats in from below. The overhead clouds are lit red-orange and a hole punches through them. At 2 s the top rises; at 3.5 s a neck and vortex ring form; the stem twists left-handed; two fog rings appear above the column. The cauliflower ball goes orange, then dull red by about 30 s, with a violet-purple radioluminescent glow for about 5 s and a faint purple haze. The red-brown cloud whitens as it climbs, pauses at the inversion (about 3.8 km), and reaches about 10.5 km in three layers: a low dust sheet drifting NE, a mid inversion layer, and a 4.5 km cap drifting slowly NW. The cloud top catches pink sunrise light at about 20 min. Afterwards: tower vaporised; 70 m bowl inside a 350 m saucer inside a 600 m light-green trinitite disc; Jumbo intact about 730 m away.
disputes_resolved: (1) Yield: use 21 kt (official). 24.8 +/- 2 kt overlaps 21 +/- 2, would break the order (Baker 23 kt), and changes the visible size by only 7%. Low blast/Fermi/preprint values under-count. (2) Cloud top: contemporaneous instrumented figures are 35-41 kft MSL (DASA 1251 35 kft and still rising; Groves 41 kft MSL = 36 kft AGL; LANL 38 kft), i.e. 9.3-11.0 km AGL. The 50-70 kft (Warren, 'variously estimated') figure is rejected. Game value 10.5 km AGL. (3) Crater: the figures describe nested features. Groves memo bowl 130 ft x 6 ft; Wikipedia 80 m x 1.4 m; DASA 1,100 ft x 9.5 ft saucer; NPS half-mile fused zone; 28 h aerial photo with scale bar shows an 80-100 m bowl and a 600 m dark disc. Game: 70 m x 1.8 m bowl / 350 m saucer / 600 m trinitite. (4) Radius vs time: use Taylor/Mack 130 m @25 ms and 175 m @53 ms, not the physics doc's 138/200. (5) Colours: violet-white flash, white, yellow, orange-red, dull red, purple glow. 'Purple-green-white' is not supported in Smith's own words; green is mostly a welding-glass artifact (Morrison). (6) Skirt, spikes and Mach belt are confirmed by Mack in LA-6300-H. (7) Time: 05:29:45 MWT (minority figure 05:29:21). (8) Sound at 9 km is about 27 s, not 40 s (40-45 s is the 16 km base-camp figure).
blurb_ru: 16 июля 1945 года в 05:29 по местному времени, ещё до рассвета, в пустыне Нью-Мексико на 30-метровой стальной башне взорвали первое в истории ядерное устройство — «Gadget». Официальная мощность — 21 кт (анализ LANL 2021 года даёт 24,8 ± 2 кт). Вспышка на секунды осветила горы ярче дня, облако поднялось выше 10 км. Жар оплавил песок в зелёное стекло, которое назвали тринититом.
blurb_en: On 16 July 1945 at 05:29 local time, before dawn, the first nuclear device in history, the "Gadget", was set off on a 30 m steel tower in the New Mexico desert. Its official yield is 21 kt; a 2021 Los Alamos re-analysis gives 24.8 ± 2 kt. For a few seconds the flash lit the mountains brighter than day, and the cloud rose more than 10 km. The heat fused the desert sand into green glass, later named trinitite.

date: 1946-07-25 08:35 local PPG time (1946-07-24 21:35 UTC), Bikini lagoon
yield_status: MEASURED/official 23 kt (DASA-1251, Wikipedia, NWA); older captions say 21 kt; Glasstone says 'approximately 20 kt'. Game: 23 kt.
burst_type: Shallow underwater: device hung from LSM-60 in mid-lagoon
paint: Not documented for 'Helen of Bikini'. It was a Mk III Fat Man-type device with no tail fins, inside a steel caisson made from a submarine conning tower, so it is never seen. For an info card, use the Nagasaki Fat Man scheme: mustard yellow with black asphalt sealant on the seams (by analogy).
key_timings: No fireball in air. 0-0.02 s: blue-white glow seen under water. 4 ms: spray dome starts at 760 m/s. 0-1 s: dark slick ring (~1,500 m/s) followed by a white crack disk. 0.75 s: column top at 640 m. Wilson cloud: visible from 0.5 s, a 1.6 km white hemisphere at 1.2-1.5 s, clears from the water up by 3-3.5 s; remnant sheet at cloud base fades by ~15 s. Column: 600 m wide, ~90 m walls (estimated), ~1.8 km high (estimated). Cloud top: 1.14 km at 5 s, 1.4 km at 10 s, 1.8 km at 30 s, 2.32 km at 60 s, ~3.0 km max. Cauliflower width: 1.5 km at 5 s, 2.6 km at 60 s. First wave: 28.7 m trough-to-crest at 305 m and 11 s; H·R = 8,730 m^2; reaches 610 m at 23 s, 1.22 km at 48 s, 3.66 km at 154 s, Bikini beach (5.6 km) at 306 s. Base surge starts 10-12 s at R = 320-370 m; R(t) = (3600+3700t)/(90+t) m (370 m at 10 s, 920 m at 30 s, 1,440 m at 60 s, 2,140 m at 120 s, 2,560 m at 200 s; stops ~240 s); height 130 m at 10 s, 300 m at 60 s, 550 m from 140 s. Cauliflower falls from 12 s; rain reaches the sea at ~1 min; head gone by 2.5 min. Surge lifts at ~210 s (base 460 m up at 4.5 min), becomes a grey stratocumulus deck up to ~1.8 km; rain for ~1 h.
visual_signature: Water burst with no fireball and no flash. (1) A brief blue-white glow under the lagoon (<20 ms). A dark slick ring races out at ~1.5 km/s, followed by a white crack disk; a white spray dome erupts at 760 m/s with a glint of fireball light on top. (2) A hollow white-grey column ~600 m wide shoots up with a ragged crown (640 m by 0.75 s). (3) From 0.5 s a smooth milky-white Wilson hemisphere, 1.6 km wide and 0.8 km tall, swallows the column; only the crown pokes through, and a white shock disk lies on the water. From ~2 s it thins bottom-up (dome → disk → ring) and is gone near the water by ~3.5 s; a flat remnant sheet at cumulus base fades by ~15 s. (4) 3-12 s: the column stands revealed, white-grey with grey-brown sediment streaks and spike jets out of its walls, capped by a lumpy white-to-light-grey cauliflower with a faint tan tint (1.5 km wide at 5 s). (5) At 9-11 s a ±14 m breaking ring wave hits ships at ~300 m (a carrier stern rises 13 m), followed by a train of up to 20 concentric waves. (6) From 10-12 s the outer column shell collapses in dark slate-grey hanging lobes and rain curtains. A brilliant white ground-hugging fog wall (the base surge) bursts out from R ≈ 350 m at 37 m/s, grows to 1.44 km radius and 300 m high at 60 s, and reaches 2.56 km radius and 550 m high at 3-4 min. It is doughnut-shaped with a clear centre after ~1 min, slightly egg-shaped downwind, and ships vanish inside it. (7) The head rains out by 2.5 min (top 2.3 km at 60 s, ~3 km max). From ~3.5 min the surge lifts off the sea into a grey stratocumulus deck with rain shafts for ~1 h; the lagoon is covered in swell rings and 2-5 m surf hits Bikini beach at ~5 min. Palette: turquoise/navy lagoon, pure white dome/Wilson cloud/surge, white-grey column, dark slate lobes. No orange or red at any stage. Sun 39° up in the ENE, light SE wind, humid air with scattered cumulus.
disputes_resolved: Lagoon depth: use 55 m (180 ft). DASA-1251 and NPS say the device was 90 ft down and 90 ft above the floor; Glasstone's '200 ft' is rounding; no source for 70 m was found. Yield: 23 kt rather than 21. Wilson cloud: visible from 0.5 s, full at 1.2-1.5 s, gone near the water by 3-3.5 s (Glasstone 1-2 s for the 1946 tests generally; column hidden ~2 s; NOL slide shows a hemisphere at ~0.8 s). Cloud top: 2.3 km at 60 s (DASA) and ~3.0 km max while dispersing (Glasstone); both are right at different times. Cauliflower width 1.8 vs 2.6 km is time-dependent: 1.5 km at 5 s, 2.6 km at 60 s. First wave '94 ft' is crest-to-trough, so the crest is ~+14 m. Base surge '3.5 miles across' vs measured 2.56 km mean radius: use 5.1 km diameter. Water lifted 1 vs 2 Mt: use ~1 Mt (Glasstone). Ships sunk 8 vs 10: say 'several' in the UI. Lagoon crater: 1,000 × 550 m, 7.6 m deep (DASA/NPS) vs 610 m × 9 m (Wikipedia); it is underwater and invisible anyway.
blurb_ru: 25 июля 1946 года в лагуне атолла Бикини заряд типа «Толстяк» мощностью 23 кт взорвали на глубине 27 м под десантным кораблём LSM-60. Взрыв выбросил полый столб воды шириной около 600 м и высотой до ~1,8 км; на пару секунд его скрыло белое конденсационное облако Вильсона диаметром около 1,6 км. Волна высотой 29 м (от подошвы до гребня) и радиоактивная «базисная волна» водяного тумана накрыли флот-мишень. Затонули линкор «Арканзас», авианосец «Саратога» и ещё несколько кораблей.
blurb_en: On 25 July 1946, in Bikini lagoon, a 23-kiloton Fat Man-type charge was fired 27 m underwater beneath the landing ship LSM-60. It threw up a hollow column of water about 600 m wide and up to ~1.8 km high, hidden for a couple of seconds by a white, mile-wide Wilson condensation cloud. A 29 m (trough-to-crest) wave and a radioactive "base surge" of mist swept the target fleet, sinking the battleship Arkansas, the carrier Saratoga and several other ships.

date: 1962-07-06 10:00 PDT (17:00:00 UTC; written '0900 PST' in DNA 6029F), Nevada Test Site Area 10, Yucca Flat
yield_status: MEASURED/official 104 kt (DNA 6029F, NRHP, DOE/NV-712, Wikipedia; preliminary 100 ± 15 kt). Thermonuclear, fission under 30%.
burst_type: Buried cratering shot (shallow underground, optimum cratering depth) in desert alluvium with ~7% water
paint: Not documented. The device was never visible: buried 635 ft down a 91 cm cased shaft backfilled with sand. Do not render; show a shaft cutaway on the info card if wanted.
key_timings: 0.24 s: shock reaches the surface; ground spalls at ~32 m/s and a wide tan dust haze jumps off. 0.45 s: rarefaction returns. 1.3 s: gas acceleration takes over; ~40 m/s by 2.0 s. Dome height keyframes (interpolated): 0.5 s ≈ 8 m, 1 s ≈ 20 m, 1.5 s ≈ 33 m, 2 s ≈ 52 m, 2.5 s ≈ 72 m, 3.0 s ≈ 88-91 m, 180-250 m wide (measured at ~3 s). Venting with an incandescent glow at 3.0-4.0 s (measured: 'secondary explosion and flash' at ~3 s; NWA 'shortly before 4 s'). Ejecta fountain to ~610 m (measured), apex ~12-15 s (estimated); clods land out to ~1.7 km. Fallback and base surge from ~10-20 s (estimated). Base surge final extent ~4 km crosswind / 3.2 km upwind (measured); timing estimated at ~1 km at 40-60 s, ~2 km at 1.5-2 min, ~3 km at 3 min, final at 4-6 min. Main dust cloud 3.7 km AGL (measured top), reached at ~5-6 min (estimated); drifts N-NNE at ~19 km/h; dust over GZ until ~H+1 h. Crater 370 m (apparent) / 390 m (lip crest) × 98 m; lip 6-30 m; magnitude 4.75.
visual_signature: No fireball, flash or condensation cloud. Clear blue sky, flat tan creosote desert, sun 51° up in the east. (1) At 0.24 s the ground over GZ suddenly shudders and a thin tan dust haze jumps off a 400-600 m disc. (2) 1.3-3 s: a smooth pale-tan dome swells to ~90 m high and ~200 m wide, cracking radially with dust streaming from the cracks. (3) At ~3-4 s the dome bursts. A dull salmon-orange/peach incandescent glow shows through the vents for 1-2 s; this is the only 'fire' in the event. The dome explodes into a spiky bush of dark clods. (4) 4-15 s: a dark grey-brown lumpy ejecta column rises to ~610 m, and dozens of cream-white ballistic streamers (clods trailing dust) arc out and down like a fountain or palm crown; blocks land out to ~1.7 km with small dust puffs. (5) From ~10-20 s the fallback curtain crashes down and launches a ground-hugging beige-grey dust base surge, 100-300 m tall, at ~30-50 m/s. It slows as it spreads, reaching ~4 km radius crosswind (3.2 km upwind) at ~4-6 min, 200-500 m tall, and is wider than the main cloud. (6) A grey-brown cauliflower-textured dust tower with no cap rises to 3.7 km above ground by ~5-6 min, flattens under an inversion, lightens and drifts north. Dust hides GZ for ~1 h. (7) Revealed crater: a clean conical pale-tan funnel 370 m across at the original ground (lip crest ~390-400 m) and 98 m deep, with a hummocky 6-30 m lip, radial ejecta dunes and rays out to ~1.7 km, and scattered splash craters. Palette: blue sky, tan/ochre desert, pale-tan dome, dark slate/grey-brown column, cream streamers, beige-grey surge, brief salmon-orange vent glow, bone-tan crater.
disputes_resolved: Crater diameter: model a 370 m apparent rim and a ~390-400 m lip crest. NRHP gives 1,214 ft, Glasstone radius 611 ft, and PNE-203F and PNE-213F ~1,200 ft; DOE fact sheet and Wikipedia give 1,280 ft = 390 m, likely lip crest or rounded. UI: '≈370-390 m'. Depth: 98 m (320-323 ft), not 100 m. Cloud height: 3.7 km AGL (12,000 ft above the desert floor per PNE-203F and DNA 6029F); Wikipedia's 16,000 ft is MSL (ground ~4,300 ft) and UPI's 15,000 ft is a press estimate. Venting: dome break-up at 3.0 s, glow over 3-4 s. Device mass: 212 kg (Sublette/Wikipedia) vs 158 kg (sonicbomb); use 212, cosmetic only. Time: 09:00 PST = 10:00 PDT = 17:00 UTC, the same instant; use 10:00 local. Base-surge and main-cloud growth timings are ESTIMATED (only final extents are documented).
blurb_ru: 6 июля 1962 года на Невадском полигоне по программе мирных ядерных взрывов «Плаушер» термоядерный заряд мощностью 104 кт взорвали на глубине 194 м в пустынном грунте. За 3 секунды земля вспучилась куполом высотой около 90 м, затем сквозь трещины вырвались раскалённые газы, и в воздух взлетело около 11 млн тонн грунта. Осталась воронка «Седан» диаметром около 370–390 м и глубиной 98 м — крупнейший рукотворный кратер в США.
blurb_en: On 6 July 1962, at the Nevada Test Site, the Plowshare peaceful-explosions programme fired a 104-kiloton thermonuclear charge buried 194 m deep in desert alluvium. Within 3 seconds the ground swelled into a dome about 90 m high, then glowing gases burst through and some 12 million short tons (≈11 million tonnes) of earth were hurled skyward. It left Sedan Crater, about 370-390 m across and 98 m deep: the largest man-made crater in the United States.

date: 1952-11-16 11:30 local (1952-11-15 23:30 GMT), Enewetak Atoll, 610 m north of Runit Island
yield_status: MEASURED, official 500 kt (DNA 6036F, NWA, Wikipedia). The 550 ± 20 kt figure was not found in any source.
burst_type: free-fall airburst over reef/lagoon (very low scaled height, 57 m/kt^1/3)
paint: Undocumented for the test unit. DESIGN: Mk 6-style olive-drab ribbed casing with a yellow nose cap and yellow bands (as on museum Mk 6 casings), labelled as a reconstruction.
key_timings: t_min ≈0.05 s; second thermal max ≈0.64 s; max fireball ≈5.6 s (R≈650 m, flattened on the sea); 90% thermal by ≈8 s; Wilson cloud ≈0.5–5 s; cloud 8.5 km and cap 3.4 km wide at 60 s (measured); ≈20 km and cap ≈12 km at ≈4 min; top 23 km, base 12 km, cap 27 km at ≈10 min (measured); shock at Parry Island (≈18 km) at 45 s (measured); at 50 km ≈136 s.
visual_signature: Midday tropical sky, low trade cumulus, burst 450 m above a turquoise reef. Blue-white flash; dip at 0.05 s with an orange shell; white peak at 0.64 s; the fireball grows to ≈1.3 km wide by ≈5.6 s with a flattened, glaring contact patch on the water, a racing white spray and Mach-stem ring, and a circular shock scar through the cumulus deck. A bright condensation dome and discs (R≈1.2–2 km) flash 0.5–5 s and light the cloud deck yellow. From 8 s it rises as an orange-red torus with a dark red-brown top and a thin reddish spray stem; smoke-rocket trails bend. 60 s: cap 8.5 km high, 3.4 km wide, orange glow inside brown. 45 s at 18 km: one hard gun-like crack. 4 min: ≈20 km, 12 km wide, brown turning white-grey. 10 min: top 23 km (tropopause 18 km), base 12 km, cap 27 km, spreading in long streaks to W/SE/SW and leaving a high thin overcast. No crater; fires and flooding on nearby islets.
disputes_resolved: Cloud top: 23 km final (75–76 kft in two independent analyses, Hubert/Machta 1953 and Castle Project 9.1 1954). The 19.8 km (65 kft, at ≈4 min) and 20.4 km (67 kft, early report) are earlier-time values. Cap diameter: measured 3.4 km @1 min and 27.4 km @10 min; the 12 km '4 min' value fits the log-interpolation, so D(t)=3.4 km·(t/1 min)^0.91. Base 12 km (two sources). Yield 500 kt. Fireball radius ≈650 m > 450 m burst height, so its lower part flattens on the sea surface (estimated).
blurb_ru: Ivy King — самый мощный взрыв бомбы деления (без термоядерной ступени) в истории США: 500 килотонн. 16 ноября 1952 года бомбардировщик B-36 сбросил бомбу Mk 18 над рифом атолла Эниветок, и она взорвалась на высоте около 450 м. Облако поднялось примерно до 23 км, а ударная волна дошла до наблюдателей в 18 км примерно через 45 секунд.
blurb_en: Ivy King was the most powerful pure-fission explosion the United States ever set off: 500 kilotons. On 16 November 1952 a B-36 dropped a Mk 18 bomb over the reef of Enewetak Atoll, and it burst about 450 m up. The cloud climbed to about 23 km, and the blast reached observers 18 km away roughly 45 seconds later.

name_en: B83 (1.2 Mt, modelled laydown surface burst)
name_ru: B83 (1,2 Мт, условная модель наземного взрыва)
date: In service since 1983 (about 650 built); never detonated in the atmosphere (underground tests from 15 Dec 1984); slated for retirement but still in the stockpile in 2026
yield_status: MEASURED: official public maximum 1.2 Mt (variable yield). The explosion itself is ESTIMATED (Glasstone scaling, cross-checked against Castle Nectar, a 1.69 Mt surface burst).
burst_type: parachute-retarded laydown, delayed contact surface burst (design decision per task)
paint: Gloss white with small black/red stencils (trainers, museum examples and service photos). The 1983 flight-test unit was high-visibility red-orange. Parachute colour undocumented: DESIGN orange-and-white ribbons.
key_timings: Chute (14 m Kevlar-nylon ribbon, 3 pilot chutes) slows the bomb to ≈20 m/s within seconds of a release as low as 46 m; lies on the ground and detonates after a delay (DESIGN 10–30 s). t_min ≈0.08 s (hemisphere R_breakaway ≈750 m); second max ≈0.95 s; max hemisphere R≈1.25 km at ≈9–10 s; 90% thermal ≈11 s; cloud 7.5 km and cap 6 km at 60 s; ≈15 km at 3 min; cap ≈20 km at 4 min; top 21 km, base 12 km, cap 35 km at ≈10 min. Shock: 5 km ≈8 s, 10 km ≈20 s, 20 km ≈48 s, 55 km ≈150 s. 5 psi ≈6 km, 1 psi ≈19 km.
visual_signature: Generic dry plain, clear sky. A low-flying jet releases the white ring-nosed bomb; three pilot chutes, then a 14 m ribbon canopy; the bomb thuds down nose-first and lies under the collapsing chute. Ground-level blue-white flash; red-orange hemisphere ≈1.5 km wide at 0.1 s; blinding white dome at ≈1 s with the ground igniting and a dense dust skirt; grows to a 2.5 km wide yellow-orange hemisphere at ≈9 s with a dark dusty fringe; a short condensation dome if humid; a bright dust line of shock runs across the plain. From 10 s the fireball lifts as a red-brown torus, pulling up a thick dark-brown soil stem (3–4 km wide at the base) while debris rains back. 60 s: cap 7.5 km, 6 km wide, red-brown. 4 min: ≈15–19 km, 20 km wide, brown-grey. 10 min: top 21 km, base 12 km, 35 km wide, dirty grey-brown, with a dark fallout curtain downwind. Leaves a crater ≈300 m wide and ≈75 m deep, a 19 m lip and a ≈660 m grey ejecta blanket. At 55 km: ground tremor first, then a long deep boom at ≈2.5 min.
disputes_resolved: Dimensions 12 ft x 18 in agree across three sources (NWA, Hill AFB fact sheet, Allbombs). Mass 2,400–2,465 lb, so 1,100 kg. Paint: white (trainer/museum); red-orange belongs to the test body only. No atmospheric test exists, so all explosion values are ESTIMATED. Crater from Glasstone §6.09 W^0.3 in dry soil: R 153 m, depth 77 m, lip 19 m, ejecta to R≈330 m, ±30%. In wet coral it would be about 3x wider. Cloud: equatorial curve 24 km vs Castle Nectar (1.69 Mt surface) measured 21.9 km; game uses 21 km.
blurb_ru: B83 — самая мощная бомба, остававшаяся в арсенале США в 2020-х годах: мощность регулируется, максимум 1,2 мегатонны. В атмосфере её не взрывали ни разу (заряд испытывали только под землёй), поэтому здесь показана расчётная модель: бомба опускается на 14-метровом парашюте, ложится на землю и взрывается с задержкой. По формулам Гласстона такой наземный взрыв оставил бы воронку около 300 м в поперечнике.
blurb_en: The B83 is the most powerful bomb still in the US arsenal in the 2020s, with a variable yield of up to 1.2 megatons. It has never been exploded in the atmosphere (its nuclear explosive was tested only underground), so this is a calculated model: the bomb descends on a 14-metre parachute, lies on the ground and detonates after a delay. Glasstone's scaling gives such a surface burst a crater roughly 300 m across.

date: 1955-11-22, release 09:47 from a Tu-16 at 12 km over experimental field P5, Semipalatinsk test site (detonation after the parachute descent)
yield_status: MEASURED: 1.6 Mt (test commission, 24 Nov 1955, VNIIEF 1997). Design ≈3 Mt, deliberately reduced. Some secondary sources say 1.6–1.9 Mt.
burst_type: parachute-retarded airburst
paint: Undocumented. DESIGN: dark olive-grey, flagged as a reconstruction. Documented: the Tu-16A carrier had its lower surfaces stripped of lacquer and all dark surfaces painted special white. PG-4083 parachute look undocumented (DESIGN white or orange-white round canopy).
key_timings: t_min ≈0.09 s; second max ≈1.1 s; max fireball R≈1.0 km at ≈10 s (base ≈0.5 km above the ground; underside flattened by the ground-reflected shock from ≈2–4 s); flash seen by the crew for 10–12 s (measured); Wilson dome 0.5–6 s; condensation bell skirt on the stem ≈30–120 s; cap enters the overcast (8.5–10 km) within 1–2 min; 14 km at ≈3 min; top ≈20 km, base ≈13 km, cap 28 km at ≈7–8 min. Shock: 35 km ≈90 s as a double thunderclap; 70 km ≈3 min with a multiple rumble; the aircraft was hit 224 s after release (2.5 g).
visual_signature: Frozen feather-grass steppe under a solid grey two-layer overcast topping out at 10 km; low winter light. A white-patched Tu-16 releases at 12 km and the bomb descends under a large round parachute. The flash lights the overcast from below; a yellow-white sphere swells and turns orange within a fraction of a second; second peak at ≈1.1 s, ≈1.5 km wide. A large Wilson condensation dome and discs (R≈2–3 km) flash 0.5–6 s. The ground-reflected shock flattens the fireball's underside, a dusty Mach ring races outward and raises a broad low billowing dust skirt. By ≈10 s: an orange fireball ≈2 km wide, base 0.5 km above the ground; the flash is over by 10–12 s. Then a glowing orange-red torus rises, pulling a thin dark twisting dust stem from the centre of the dust cloud. The cap is red-brown with crimson glints (Sakharov: swirling grey-blue cloud with crimson flashes) and punches into the overcast within 1–2 min. A translucent bell-shaped condensation skirt forms around the mid-stem (≈half the cap's width), with thin rings where the stem crosses the humid layers. At 35 km, ≈90 s: two sharp thunder-like cracks and ear pressure, grass flattened. At 70 km, ≈3 min: windows blown in, a long multiple rumble. The inversion-bent shock breaks glass far away. From the air: top ≈20 km, base ≈13 km, cap 28 km at ≈7 min, red-brown turning grey-blue. Later the dust merges with the overcast into a lead-black storm cloud drifting at azimuth ≈70°. No crater.
disputes_resolved: Burst height 1,550 m (VNIIEF 1997 p. 234 and four other sources); 2,000 m appears in only one secondary listing and is rejected. Cloud: the documented '13–14 km at 5–7 min' is pre-stabilisation, partly obscured by overcast, and probably the cap base. VNIIEF's crew report 'lower boundary 1200–1400 m' is likely a dropped zero for 12–14 km. A 25–30 km cap implies a top of ≈20–25 km, and the mid-latitude November atmosphere reduces rise below the equatorial 24–25 km. So base 13 km, top 20 km, cap 28 km. Condensation ring/skirt confirmed (VNIIEF 'large condensation regions' plus published photo). Double thunder confirmed by the primary report at 35 km; cause not stated, likely two acoustic paths via the inversion (estimated). Inversion focusing confirmed (Sakharov memoir; damage in 59 settlements; 28,615 m² of glass; injuries in Semipalatinsk city about 200 km away). 09:47 is the release time. The girl died in Malye Akzhary (VNIIEF), not Kurchatov. Length 5.87–7 m disputed, so 6.0 m approximate.
blurb_ru: РДС-37 — первая советская двухступенчатая водородная бомба. 22 ноября 1955 года её сбросили с самолёта Ту-16 на парашюте над Семипалатинским полигоном, и на высоте 1550 м она взорвалась с мощностью 1,6 Мт (расчётная мощность около 3 Мт была намеренно снижена). Температурная инверсия отразила ударную волну обратно к земле: пострадали строения в 59 населённых пунктах, погибли два человека.
blurb_en: RDS-37 was the first Soviet two-stage hydrogen bomb. On 22 November 1955 a Tu-16 dropped it by parachute over the Semipalatinsk test site, and it exploded 1,550 m up with 1.6 megatons (the planned ~3 Mt was deliberately reduced). A temperature inversion bent the shock wave back to the ground, damaging buildings in 59 settlements and killing two people.

yield_status: MEASURED: 10.4 Mt (DOE/NV, Sublette, DNA 6036F, DTRA 2013). Fireball-yield measurement in the Castle Project 9.1 table: 11 ± 1 Mt.
burst_type: surface (stationary device inside a shot-cab building on Elugelab islet)
paint: Not a bomb. The 'Sausage' was a vertical cylinder, 80 in (2.03 m) wide x 244 in (6.2 m) tall, 82 short tons with its cryogenic plant. The colour photo shows bright, unpainted silver metal with large horizontal pipes. It stood inside a 27 x 14 x 19 m corrugated-aluminium shot cab, with a 91 m signal tower and a 2.7 km conduit/causeway to Boken. The UI must not call it a bomb.
key_timings: 0.005-0.08 s: five lightning channels rise from the sea ~1 km from GZ (measured on film). 1 s: fireball ~4.5 km wide (Sedov-Taylor estimate). ~3-5 s: max ~5.2 km ('like the sun half-risen'), with a huge Wilson cloud and low scud partly hiding it. 5-15 s: hover, then lift-off. 10-90 s: curtain of water around the stem base. 60 s: top ~13 km (measured 11.9-14.2 km), cap 9 km wide. 90 s: 17 km. ~2.5 min: sound/shock at ships ~50 km away. 2.6 min: ~30-33 km. 3.5 min: 33 km. 5.7 min: ~36 km. Then the main top stays at ~36.6 km (120,000 ft) for about 1 h; optional plume to 41 km. Cap: 61 km @10 min, ~97-100 km @30 min (stem/lower cloud 32 km wide, junction ~14 km); 161 km only as an eventual spread. Cap underside ~20 km.
visual_signature: Sunrise, sun +2 deg in the ESE, scattered trade cumulus at 0.6-2 km, a tiny flat islet with a metal shed and a tower. t=0: blue-white white-out; within 10 ms five jagged lightning bolts from the sea about 1 km out. 0-1 s: a flat-based white hemisphere with a mottled surface, ~4.5 km wide. 1-5 s: it grows to ~5.2 km, a dome 'like the sun half-risen' on the horizon, white to yellow-white; a huge white Wilson condensation cloud (~6-10 km, estimated) flashes over it and the low clouds partly hide it. 5-15 s: brief hover, then lift; the colour shifts yellow-orange to orange-red with dark veins. 10-90 s: a ring curtain of spray rises around the base and falls back; a wide, dirty grey-brown stem ~3-4 km; a toroidal cauliflower cap, brilliant white on the sunlit side, lights the cumulus below orange; top 13 km at 60 s, 17 km at 90 s, punching through the tropopause. 2.5-6 min: the rise slows (30 km at 2.5 min, 36 km at 5.5 min) and the cap 'splashes' flat; white cap with reddish-brown tints in the shadowed folds; smooth pileus sheets cut across the stem. 6-10 min: main top ~37 km, underside ~20 km, optional thin turret to 41 km; cap 61 km wide at 10 min. 10-30 min: the cap spreads to ~100 km; the lower stem broadens to ~30 km with 'projecting fingers' at the ~14 km junction. Ground: the islet is gone, leaving a 1.9 km x 50 m water-filled crater; neighbouring islets are swept bare; a 1 m wave reaches Enewetak Island ~30 min later.
disputes_resolved: (1) Ceiling 36.6 vs 41 km: 36.6 km (120,000 ft) is the main top, from 1953 AFOAT-1 aircraft sextant data that stayed constant for an hour, the official DNA 6036F history ('over 120,000 ft', later questioned) and Sublette. 41 km (135,500 ft) is a single sighting of a sharp plume above the top. The 1954 Castle photogrammetric comparison gives only 98,000 ft (30 km), so the true main top was probably 30-37 km. Game: 37 km main top, optional turret to 41 km. (2) Cap width 100-160 km: no measured time is attached to these figures. Measured: 9 km @1 min, 61 km @10 min (EG&G/Castle 9.1 table), ~97 km ('sixty miles') @30 min (TG 132.1 history). '100 miles' is the 1953 film's rounded figure. Game: 61 km @10 min, 100 km @30 min. (3) Fireball 5.2 km: the official film says 'at its maximum about 3 1/4 miles'; NNSA caption 3 1/2 mi; Wikipedia's 2.9-3.3 km radius comes from the Fourmilab calculator, not a measurement. Game: 5.2 km max at ~3-5 s. (4) Rise timing: 12-14 km @60 s, 17 km @90 s, ~30-33 km @2.6 min, ~36 km @5.7 min. Wikipedia's 'one minute later 33 km' means 33 km at ~2.6 min.
blurb_ru: Первый в мире термоядерный взрыв: это была 74-тонная установка в здании на островке Элугелаб (атолл Эниветок), а не бомба. 1 ноября 1952 года мощность 10,4 Мт дала огненный шар шириной около 5 км, а облако поднялось примерно на 37 км и за полчаса раскинулось почти на 100 км. Остров исчез — на его месте осталась подводная воронка диаметром 1,9 км и глубиной около 50 м.
blurb_en: The world's first thermonuclear explosion came from a 74-tonne device housed in a building on Elugelab islet (Enewetak Atoll), not from a bomb. On 1 November 1952 its 10.4-megaton yield made a fireball about 5 km wide, and the cloud rose to roughly 37 km and spread nearly 100 km across within half an hour. The island vanished, leaving an underwater crater 1.9 km wide and about 50 m deep.

yield_status: MEASURED: 15 Mt (DOE, Sublette, DTRA 2013, AHF). Fireball-yield measurement: 14.8 ± 0.2 Mt (Castle Project 9.1). Predicted 6 Mt (range 4-8). Wikipedia's '±5 Mt' is not supported by the measurement record.
burst_type: surface (land-surface shot on Site 20, a small artificial islet on the reef off Namu, Bikini Atoll; device in a concrete shot cab)
paint: Not a bomb: the 'SHRIMP' was a horizontal cylinder, 179.5 in (4.56 m) x 53.9 in (1.37 m), 23,500 lb (10,659 kg). The photo (LANL/DTRIAC D-92-1) shows plain, unpainted light-grey metal with rounded ends, on steel stands, with cables attached, inside a two-storey concrete cab. No markings are documented.
key_timings: 0-1 s: hemisphere ~4.8 km wide. 3.5 s: ~6 km (photo from 75 nm). ~8-10 s: max ~7 km; it 'clings to the earth', then springs up. 0.35-0.9 min: condensation rings at ~3-4 km and ~5 km altitude; ice caps with undersides at ~6 and ~7 km, 9-14 km wide; ring 3 at 8-9.7 km. 45 s: rings plus 2 ice caps visible. 60 s: top 14.3 km, cap 11.6 km wide, underside ~7 km, stem ~4 km (smoke-rocket trails). 1.0-1.6 min: 3rd ice cap 14->20 km wide at 6-7.6 km. 1.0-2.5 min: ring 4 rises 9->16 km. 1.6-4.2 min: 2 skirts (5.5-8 km high, 7->15 km wide). 1.3-6 min: 3 bells (up to 9/12/16 km wide). 2 min: top 25 km, cap 24 km. 3 min: 31 km. 4 min: 34 km, cap 44 km, underside 16 km. ~5 min: main top max 34.7 km (114,000 ft). 5.8-8 min: thunderhead dome 38-39 km (125-128 kft; 'about 130,000 ft'). ~7-8 min: sound reaches the Lucky Dragon (~160 km). 8-9 min: stem 7-8.4 km. ~8.7 min: cap 100 km. 10 min: cap 113 km (75 mi per DTRA), underside 19 km, growing ~12 km/min. ~9 min: cloud top catches direct sunlight (estimated). 16 min: anvil photo. 20-25 min: stem at 10-15 km altitude is 12-19 km wide. 30 min: sunrise left of the stem; cap ~160 km (estimated). +4-6 h: white coral fallout at Rongelap.
visual_signature: Pre-dawn (sun -8 deg in the east), deep-blue twilight, a broken trade-cumulus deck at 0.6-1.2 km, a thin cirrostratus veil, a tiny reef islet with a concrete blockhouse and a 1 km causeway. t=0: the whole sky flashes white (seen 400 km away). 0-1 s: a hemisphere ~4.8 km wide on the reef. 1-10 s: it grows to ~6 km at 3.5 s and ~7 km max at ~8-10 s, white to yellow-white, hugging the reef; the sea, cumulus deck and sky glow crimson-orange ('flaming sunset colors'); pileus caps form over the dome. 10-60 s: the fireball springs up, a yellow core with an orange boiling cauliflower surface. Signature look: several flat, thin, stacked condensation rings/discs at ~3-5 km and 8-9.5 km, plus white ice-cap sheets draped over the bubble with undersides at 6-7 km, 9-14 km wide; smoke-rocket trails beside a dirty grey-brown stem ~4 km wide. 60 s: top 14 km, cap 12 km. 1-2.5 min: a 3rd ice cap 14-20 km wide; ring 4 dragged up to 16 km; 2 cone-shaped skirts and 3 bells around the stem; the glow fades to dull red inside the cap and the sky returns to twilight blue. 2.5-5 min: the top reaches 35 km; the stem flares into a trumpet; the anvil flattens on the tropopause. 5-10 min: a central thunderhead dome rises to ~39-40 km; the anvil spreads ~12 km/min to 100 km at ~8.7 min and 113 km at 10 min, underside ~19 km, stem ~8 km; virga-like curtains of debris hang under the anvil. From ~9 min the cloud top catches pink-gold sunlight above the Earth's shadow (estimated); at 30 min the sun rises beside the stem. Ground: a 2.0 km x 76 m crater blown into the reef; hours later white coral 'snow' falls downwind.
disputes_resolved: (1) Fireball '7.2 km at 1 s': the timing is too fast. DTRA 2013 says 'within seconds… more than 3 mi across'; physics gives ~4.6-5.2 km at 1 s and a Glasstone surface max (x0.85) of ~7.0 km. Game: ~4.8 km @1 s, max ~7 km @8-10 s. (2) Cloud timeline confirmed by EG&G photogrammetry (Castle Project 9.1, Fig. 5.1/Table 5.6): 14.3 km @1 min (S11: ~15 km; DTRA: 45,000 ft); main top max 34.7 km @~5 min (DTRA: 'over 115,000 ft after 5 min'); the '40 km at 6 min' is the thunderhead dome (125-128 kft @5.8-8 min). Cap 113 km @10 min (100 km @~8.7 min; DTRA 121 km); stem ~4 km @1 min -> 7-8.4 km @8-10 min. (3) Condensation features confirmed: 4 rings, 3 ice caps, 2 skirts and 3 bells, with measured heights and diameters (Project 9.1 sec. 6.1, Figs. 6.3-6.4). (4) Crater 2.0 km x 76 m confirmed by Sublette, Wikipedia and AHF ('mile-wide' in DTRA); a modern sonar survey finds it partly infilled. (5) Crimson sky: qualitatively confirmed by the DOE/NOAA colour photos and by witnesses ('flaming sunset colors', 'red and orange colors lit up the sky'). The shot was 30 min before sunrise, so after ~2 min return to blue twilight. (6) The ±5 Mt uncertainty is unsupported (14.8 ± 0.2 Mt measured).
blurb_ru: Самый мощный ядерный взрыв США: 1 марта 1954 года на рифе атолла Бикини устройство «Shrimp» дало 15 Мт — примерно в 2,5 раза больше расчётных 6 Мт. Огненный шар шириной около 7 км окрасил предрассветное небо в красно-оранжевый цвет, а облако за 10 минут поднялось почти на 40 км и раскинулось более чем на 100 км. Радиоактивные осадки накрыли атоллы Ронгелап и Утирик и японское рыболовное судно «Дайго Фукурю-мару».
blurb_en: The largest US nuclear explosion: on 1 March 1954 the 'Shrimp' device on a Bikini Atoll reef yielded 15 megatons, about 2.5 times the predicted 6 Mt. Its fireball, about 7 km wide, lit the pre-dawn sky red and orange, and within 10 minutes the cloud reached almost 40 km in height and over 100 km in width. Fallout contaminated Rongelap and Utirik atolls and the Japanese fishing boat Daigo Fukuryu Maru.

yield_status: MEASURED (official Soviet catalogue, MINATOM 1996: 24,200 kt); Western estimates range from ~20 Mt (Johnston) to 26 Mt (contemporary US estimate, FRUS Feb 1963, JOE 184)
burst_type: airburst (air drop from aircraft; not ICBM)
paint: Not published. The game uses a generic large streamlined parachute bomb with Tsar-class proportions (~8 m x ~2 m), neutral grey with a dark nose and tail, and makes no claim that it is authentic. Mass is unknown, so 0 here means unknown.
key_timings: ESTIMATED (scaled from Tsar Bomba and physics reference): breakaway ~3.5 km diameter at 0.4 s; thermal minimum 0.4 s; main thermal maximum ~4.5 s; fireball 6 km diameter at ~5-8 s; shock reaches the ground below at ~3 s; reflected shock flattens the fireball bottom at ~5-6 s; fireball top ~9 km at 15 s; luminous dome ~25 km at 40 s; glow fades by ~50-90 s; cloud top ~53 km and two-tier cap 72/55 km at ~8-10 min; shock reaches 10 km at ~14 s, 20 km at ~37 s, 50 km at ~118 s.
visual_signature: Polar night over snow-covered Novaya Zemlya: the Sun is 11.5 deg below the horizon (it never rose that day), with a faint deep-blue twilight band in the SW and stars. A blue-white flash turns the whole snow field white and then orange. At 0.4 s the fireball is a dull orange-red ball with a dark core. It then re-brightens to blinding white and grows to ~6 km across (centre at 3.75 km, bottom ~0.7 km above the snow). A snow-dust ring runs outward from ~3 s. The reflected shock flattens the fireball's underside at ~5-6 s, with no ground contact. A Wilson shell is unlikely in dry air at -20 to -30 C. Colour goes white, then yellow (~10 s), yellow-orange (~20 s) and orange-red (~45 s) as the fireball rises and rolls into a toroid (top 9 km at 15 s, 25 km at 40 s), with a thin pale stem and no dark dust. After ~1.5 min the cloud is unlit: a dark grey-blue silhouette against the twilight and stars that climbs to ~53 km and spreads into a two-tier cap ~72/55 km wide by ~10 min. There is no crater, only a melted, glazed snow-free circle at ground zero.
disputes_resolved: DATE: 24 Dec 1962 is confirmed by the official catalogue (Mikhailov 1996 via NWA), Khalturin et al. 2005 Appendix 4, Johnston, the Wikipedia 1962 test list (CMR database) and the contemporary US FRUS table (JOE 184, 24 Dec). 22 Dec appears only in the weak en-wiki 'Test 219' article; 22 Dec was a different 6.3 kt test (No. 211). '12 Dec' on the NWA Tsar Bomba page is a typo. YIELD: 24.2 Mt (official, instrument-based), bracketed by Western estimates of ~20 Mt and 26 Mt; game uses 24.2 Mt. HEIGHT: 3,750 m official against the US estimate of 3,505 m (11,500 ft); game uses 3,750 m. DELIVERY: air drop; the 'via ICBM' claim on en-wiki is wrong. LOCATION: listed as Zone C (Sukhoy Nos), but the published coordinates (73.6N 57.5E) are imprecise; the game uses the Sukhoy Nos snowy range. Visuals are not documented, so they are ESTIMATED by scaling.
blurb_ru: Испытание № 219 — 24 декабря 1962 года, Новая Земля: сброшенный с самолёта заряд взорвался на высоте 3 750 м с мощностью 24,2 мегатонны. Это второй по мощности взрыв в истории после «Царь-бомбы» — испытание 50-мегатонной конструкции на пониженной мощности. Взрыв прогремел в полярную ночь: солнце в тот день так и не поднялось над горизонтом.
blurb_en: Test No. 219 — 24 December 1962, Novaya Zemlya: an air-dropped device burst 3,750 m up with a yield of 24.2 megatons. It is the second most powerful explosion in history after the Tsar Bomba, a reduced-yield test of a 50-megaton-class design. It went off in the polar night: that day the Sun never rose above the horizon.

date: 1961-10-30 08:33:28 UT (11:33 MSK); release ~188 s earlier
yield_status: DISPUTED: 50 Mt is the official and designers' figure (Adamsky & Smirnov 1994; Mikhailov catalogue 50,000 kt). Early Russian and Western figures are 57-58 Mt (US Bethe panel 57 Mt; Johnston table 58 Mt), 58.6 Mt is quoted in ru-wiki, and up to 63 Mt (CIA 1963) or 75 Mt (first estimates). Design yield was 100 Mt. Game uses 50 Mt.
burst_type: airburst, parachute-retarded air drop from a Tu-95V at 10,500 m with a barometric fuze
paint: Not documented for the test unit. The Sarov museum casing (RDS-202 body) is bare silver-grey metal with riveted seams, a black nose cap and a black finned tail section; game uses this, labelled undocumented. The carrier Tu-95V No. 5800302 and the Tu-16A lab No. 3709 were painted overall anti-flash white, including the propellers.
key_timings: Release ~11:30:20 MSK, 188 s parachute fall, burst 11:33:28 MSK at 4.0 km AGL (4.2 km ASL). Breakaway ~4.6-5.5 km diameter at ~0.5 s; thermal minimum ~0.56 s (NWA); main maximum ~5-7 s; fireball reaches ~8 km diameter by ~5-10 s. Shock hits the ground below at ~3 s and the reflected shock strikes the fireball bottom at ~6-8 s. Fireball top reaches ~10.5 km (bomber altitude) at ~15-20 s. Luminous dome ~30 km at 40 s, then the mushroom forms (film narration). Flash and glow last a bit over a minute. Cap ~40 km wide at ~2-3 min. Cloud overshoots to ~67 km at ~8-10 min and settles to ~64 km, with a two-tier cap of 95 km (upper) and 70 km (lower) by ~10 min. Shock reaches 10 km at ~12 s, 20 km at ~34 s, Severny (55 km) at ~2 min and 100 km at ~4 min, and caught the Tu-95V at 115 km and the Tu-16 at 205 km. Radio blackout ~40 min. The pressure wave circled the globe 3 times (first circuit 36 h 27 min).
visual_signature: Arctic noon on 30 Oct: the Sun is only 2.3 deg above the southern horizon, giving low golden light and long shadows over snowy mountains and a grey sea. Thick overcast lies below the burst with a broken upper layer. A white Tu-95V drops the bomb, which descends 188 s under a huge pale parachute. A blue-white flash lights the overcast from inside until it looks translucent. At ~0.55 s the fireball is an orange-red opaque ball. It re-brightens to white and grows to ~8 km diameter, its bottom nearly touching the snow. A snow-dust ring runs out from ~3 s, and at 6-8 s the reflected shock flattens the fireball's underside and pushes it up, so it never touches the ground. Seen from the aircraft it is a huge bright orange ball rising slowly out of a gap in the clouds: white, then yellow, then orange, with its top reaching 10.5 km by ~15-20 s as it punches a widening hole in the cloud deck. A red-orange toroidal dome with a mottled surface follows, with a pale column of snow and condensation to ~10 km beneath it. The dome reaches ~30 km at 40 s and turns into a mushroom ~15-20 km wide while glowing. Over 40-70 s the glow fades to dull red and then red-brown. By 1-3 min the cloud is white-pink on its sunlit south side and blue-grey on the shadow side, 40-45 km tall with a ~40 km cap and a 10-20 km stem mostly hidden below the overcast. By 8-10 min it reaches ~67 km and settles to ~64 km, with a two-tier cap (upper ~95 km, wider and flatter; lower ~70 km) visible from 800 km. There is no crater: ground zero is levelled, glazed and snow-free, with shiny melted rock edges.
disputes_resolved: FIREBALL: 8 km is the diameter (radius 4 km). The physics check agrees: R_max 4.62 km x 0.85 megaton correction = 3.9 km radius. 'Nearly six miles' (Wellerstein) and the AiF caption (5.5 km at shock separation, then 10 km) bracket it. The '4.6 km' figure is a formula value with radius and diameter mixed up (Pravda 2009 calls it diameter, Nauka Mail.ru radius, and the Commons NWA-FAQ diagram said 4.6 then 2.3 km); it is not an observation. '10.5 km' is the ALTITUDE of the fireball's top after rising to the bomber's level, not its height. GROUND CONTACT: none; the reflected shock flattened and lifted the fireball (NWA, en/ru-wiki). CLOUD: 64 km (Adamsky & Smirnov 1994) and 67/67.3 km (VNIIEF Veselov/Veselovsky) are both from participants; game renders an overshoot to 67 km settling at ~64 km, reached within ~10 min (Wellerstein). CAP: two tiers, upper 95 km and lower 70 km (Chernyshev 2011, VNIIEF), consistent with ~60 mi (Wellerstein) and ~90 km (film narration). 'BASE 40 km': the en-wiki line misreads Pravda 2009 ('64 km high and 40 km in diameter'), so it is not a base; use it as the cap width at ~2-3 min, with stem width ~10-20 km. TIME: 08:33:27.8 UT seismic (11:33 MSK); Adamsky & Smirnov give 11:32. WEATHER: cloudy, two cloud layers, fireball seen through a gap and breaking through a thick layer (CWIHP eyewitness). SUN: +2.3 deg at azimuth 187 deg (computed). FLASH: visible ~1,000 km despite cloud; the Alaska sighting is doubtful. SHOCK: Tu-95V at 39-45 km, caught at 115 km; Severny (55 km) destroyed; windows broken at 780-900 km; circled the globe 3 times. YIELD: game uses 50 Mt. MASS: 26.5 t (ru-wiki, Veselovsky) versus 27 t (NWA). DIMENSIONS: 8.0 x 2.1 m versus Veselovsky's 8.5 x 2.0 m, which probably includes the fins.
blurb_ru: 30 октября 1961 года бомбардировщик Ту-95В сбросил над Новой Землёй 26-тонную бомбу АН602 на огромном парашюте; она взорвалась на высоте 4 км с мощностью около 50 мегатонн — это самый мощный взрыв в истории человечества. Огненный шар диаметром около 8 км не коснулся земли: его отбросила собственная отражённая ударная волна, а гриб поднялся на 64–67 км, в мезосферу. Вспышку видели почти за 1000 км, несмотря на облачность, а волна давления трижды обошла земной шар.
blurb_en: On 30 October 1961 a Tu-95V bomber dropped the 26-tonne AN602 bomb over Novaya Zemlya on a huge parachute; it burst 4 km up with a yield of about 50 megatons, the most powerful explosion in human history. The roughly 8 km fireball never touched the ground, pushed back by its own reflected shock wave, and the mushroom cloud rose 64–67 km into the mesosphere. The flash was seen almost 1,000 km away despite cloud cover, and the pressure wave circled the globe three times.
